column1: # Z8: what each file of upstream's zenoh/tests must still do against the patched graph.
# Graded by scripts/lib/z8_expectation_gate.py against the report of scripts/lib/z8_upstream_suite.py.
# Columns: name <TAB> status <TAB> min_passed <TAB> lane <TAB> reason. Measured 2026-10-30 on the tree of round 3931.
# `lane` says whether the hosted lane runs the file (`yes`) or only a person does (`no`).
# A file that does better than its row is a line to raise in the commit that made it better.

column5: all of it; the file arrived with 1.10.2 (measured on the tree of round 3976)

4 tests are ignored upstream; test_liveliness_regression_3 needs a peer's open to return only after the peers it dialled have replayed their declarations, as upstream's open.return_conditions.declares does: a peer face is now sent the end of its initial declarations and the open waits for it, so a token declared before the subscriber is no longer learnt after it

measured with a process per test, as upstream's CI runs them (each scenario module installs a process-global subscriber, so one process over the file records only scenario 1): 78 of 126 pass, all of scenarios 4, 5 and 8 and half of 3 and 7; the 48 that fail all use nodes of a multicast group (scenarios 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7): scenario 1 also needs the client node (its ten tests time out), and where a publisher is declared (pubsub, queque) a member of a group registers each other member's declaration twice, which the group side of the session has still to settle; gossip::regions_gossip failed once in a run of the whole file and passed six of six alone; each failing test waits out a minute, so a person runs it

2 tests are ignored upstream; three_node_combination lost a recipe in about one run in four until a probe stopped waiting for the lock of a lane a blocking send holds (round 4017), and passed in 8 of 8 runs after
